title: streaming: lifecycle controls for client-cancel, disconnect handling, reconnect/resume, and server timeouts
author: Maya Chen
description: Motivation: customer production workloads exposed edge cases in streaming where client-initiated cancel/disconnects and transient network disconnects led to leaked runtime state, inconsistent function/tool call termination, and poor developer experience for OpenAI-compatible clients. This PR implements lifecycle controls across the streaming stack: explicit client-cancel handling, improved server-side disconnect timeouts, reconnect/resume support for idempotent streams, and better semantics for in-flight tool/function calls. Design summary: 1) Add an explicit cancel RPC (internal) that forces immediate KV-cache eviction and per-request resource cleanup. 2) Track stream sessions with a short-lived session token so reconnects can resume only when the request is compatible (same model, prompt prefix hash, and sequence state). 3) Introduce server-side graceful-disconnect timeout (configurable) that allows short network blips to reconnect; after the timeout, the server finalizes the stream and releases resources. 4) When a client cancel is observed, abort any in-progress function/tool calls and emit a canonical terminated event to both OpenAI-compat SSE streams and Redwood streaming protocol. 5) Backwards-compatible behavior: default to previous behavior unless the customer opts into strict lifecycle via the new streaming_lifecycle config. Compatibility notes: OpenAI-compat clients will see the same SSE event shapes with additional "terminated"/"resumed" events; SDKs (Python/TS) are updated to surface reconnect and cancel helpers. Testing & verification: unit tests for session token logic, integration tests simulating network flaps and client cancel, stress tests to validate no resource leaks under high churn. Rollout plan: staged rollout behind a feature flag, enable on dedicated infra first, monitor memory/stream counts, then enable globally after 2 days of stable telemetry.

review_conversation: Samir Patel: Request changes - Can we avoid a full abort of function calls for short disconnects? Suggest wiring the graceful-disconnect timeout into call_manager to let long-running calls complete if session resumes.
Maya Chen: Reply - addressed. call_manager now checks session state and will defer abort until graceful-disconnect expires; added tests for resumed long-running calls.
Ellen Park: Comment - add a metric for resumed streams vs finalizes. Also ensure we don't expose session tokens in logs.
Maya Chen: Reply - added metrics.streaming.resumed_count and metrics.streaming.finalized_count; session tokens are now redacted in logs and only logged as hashes.
Diego Ramos: Approve - LGTM after minor nits fixed.
Samir Patel: Approve - thanks, nice tests and clear docs.

release_notes:
- Added streaming lifecycle controls: client cancel, graceful disconnect timeout, reconnect/resume semantics
- OpenAI-compat: new 'terminated' and 'resumed' SSE events
- SDK: helpers for cancel() and resume() in Python and TypeScript SDKs
- Config: new streaming_lifecycle feature flag and graceful_disconnect_timeout (default 15s)
